instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F. Cut the chicken into 1 1/2 inch pieces. Toss them in a bowl with the paprika, the cumin, the black pepper, 1 tbsp of the olive oil and 3/4 tsp of the salt.
Meanwhile, slice the mushrooms, cut the onion into half moons, chop the red pepper small and cut the green pepper into large chunks. Chop the tomatoes and mince the garlic.

Heat a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high. Add 1 tbsp of the olive oil. Add half the chicken in a single layer and leave it alone for 3 minutes, until the underside is browned. Turn the pieces and cook for 2 minutes. Transfer to a plate and repeat with the rest of the chicken.
Lower the heat to medium. Add the butter and the last 1 tbsp olive oil to the same pan. Add the mushrooms and cook for 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until they're browned.
Add the onion and red pepper and cook for 4 minutes, until soft. Add 1/2 tsp of the salt.
Add the tomato paste and stir for 1 minute, until it darkens. Add the garlic and thyme and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes and 1/2 cup water. Scrape up the browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Simmer for 5 minutes, until the tomatoes start to break down.
Return the chicken and any juices to the pan. Press the pieces into the sauce and lay the green pepper on top.

Bake for 25 minutes, until the sauce is bubbling and the green pepper has softened. You're cooking the chicken to 175°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Cut into the thickest piece: it's done when the juices run clear.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve with the crusty bread. Put the red pepper flakes on the table for anyone who wants heat.
method_notes: No version with 20 or more ratings turned up, so this is a fallback. Turkey's For Life (5 from 1 rating, read from the visible rating) leads with a clay pot method: sear the chicken, fry the vegetables, layer them over the chicken with diluted tomato paste and finish with a green pepper on top. Ozlem's Turkish Table (5 from 3 ratings) simmers a bigger pot of chicken, potato, beans and zucchini on the stove for 2 hours. Pomona follows the oven version, uses thighs instead of breast, drops the 2 hour marinade to the seasoning step, and moves the chile flakes from the marinade to the table.
